item.title: The Marked Power Spectrum as a Practical Bispectrum Measure for Galaxy Redshift Surveys
item.description: arXiv:2603.03581v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modern datasets have the precision necessary to uncover new information by including higher-order, non-Gaussian information into cosmological inference. The marked power spectrum offers access to such information while preserving the structure of two-point correlators. This approach to higher-order statistics has the advantage that many modeling questions can directly benefit from progress already made in standard cosmological analyses using the power spectrum and correlation function, while increasing the data vector size negligibly and retaining much of the degeneracy-breaking power of the bispectrum through a particular data compression. In this work, we first restructure the marked power spectrum to isolate its higher-order information and demonstrate its ability to break parameter degeneracies. We then investigate the effect of survey geometry on the marked power spectrum and find that a treatment similar to that of the power spectrum is sufficient. Additionally, we investigate the perturbative modeling and covariance structure of the marked power spectrum, shedding light on its degeneracy breaking power and cross-covariance with the power spectrum. Finally, we demonstrate that the cosmology dependence of the marked power spectrum is smooth, indicating that cosmological inference is possible by modeling the cosmology dependence through interpolation rather than analytical modeling.
item.dc:creator: Haruki Ebina, Martin White, Edmond Chaussidon

item.title: Mitigating residual foregrounds and systematic errors in SKA1-Low AA* EoR observations via Bayesian Gaussian Process Regression
item.description: arXiv:2605.10928v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The redshifted 21-cm line is an emerging tool in observational cosmology that can serve as a direct probe of the intergalactic medium throughout the cosmic timeline. However, the observation of the cosmological 21-cm signal is extremely challenging in practice, regardless of the scale of interest and redshift, due to the presence of astrophysical foregrounds and residual systematic errors. Machine-learning-based Gaussian process regression (ML-GPR) has proven to be the most effective strategy for signal separation in LOFAR and NenuFAR observations to measure the 21-cm signal power spectrum from the Cosmic Dawn (CD) and Epoch of Reionization (EoR). In this work, we extend this framework to synthetic CD/EoR SKA1-Low observations to assess its robustness in mitigating residual foregrounds against instrumental and environmental systematic effects. We use our developed end-to-end realistic simulation pipeline (21cmE2E) for SKA-Low observations. Our 4-hour tracking simulation includes extragalactic point sources, the AA* telescope configuration, primary beam response, and residual systematics. The modelled errors incorporate antenna-based gain calibration errors, ionospheric phase errors, partial de-mixing of the out-of-field sources, and instrumental noise for 1000 hours of deep integration time. This work is one of the first demonstrations of the efficacy of the ML-GPR method in a realistic observing scenario. We compare different Bayesian GPR frameworks to assess their ability to suppress residual foreground contamination while minimising signal loss and providing reliable uncertainty estimates. Our results demonstrate that even in a realistic scenario where observations have a combination of residual systematics, ML-GPR can recover the 21-cm signal robustly within the $2\sigma$ confidence interval across almost the entire range of k-modes sampled.
item.dc:creator: Samit Kumar Pal, Abhirup Datta, Aishrila Mazumder, Anshuman Tripathi

item.title: Beyond Self-Similarity: Reconciling X-Ray Scaling Relations in Galaxy Clusters and Groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.02719v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Scaling relations hold among observed quantities that describe the thermodynamic properties of the gas in galaxy clusters and groups. However, observed data show systematic departures from the self-similar model's baseline predictions, particularly in lower-mass systems. I show that the observed departures from self-similar predictions can be efficiently described by two physical quantities modeled with power laws: the gas mass fraction $f_g$ and the temperature variation $f_T$. Using a wide range of published X-ray scaling relations, this study conducts an MCMC-based meta-analysis to constrain the temperature- and redshift-dependence of the meta-parameters $f_g$ and $f_T$ and calibrate the model. These calibrations indicate that, while the gas mass fraction does not show significant evolution with cosmic time, it decreases significantly with decreasing halo mass. On the other hand, the temperature variation shows a mild positive increase with both mass and redshift. Overall, modeling the departures from the self-similar model with $\{f_g, f_T\}$ drastically improves predictive accuracy, reducing the number of scaling relations in $>3\sigma$ ($>5 \sigma$) tension from 49 (36) percent under the self-similar scenario to just 8 (3) percent (three and one out of 39, respectively) that might be identified for their peculiarity. Moreover, modeling through this generalized framework allows for an extended discussion of the expected slopes and redshift evolution for several X-ray scaling laws, including the new quantity $Y_{LGT0} = L^{-1} M_g^2 T^{a_L}$, a proxy for the cluster's volume that is independent of $f_g$ and $f_T$ by construction, and is predicted to scale directly with mass with a well-defined redshift evolution ($M \sim Y_{LGT0} f_g^0 f_T^0 E_z^2$), as validated against hydrodynamical simulations and observational constraints.
item.dc:creator: S. Ettori (INAF-OAS Bologna)

item.title: Dark Energy Survey Year 3 results: optimized $w$CDM simulation-based inference with weak lensing map-level hybrid statistics
item.description: arXiv:2606.11309v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present cosmological constraints from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 (DES Y3) weak lensing data using hierarchical hybrid statistics within a Bayesian simulation-based inference framework that is based on the Gower Street simulations. To maximize the precision of the inference, we have developed a new, information-theory based, data compression of the weak lensing maps to just seven highly informative summary statistics. The hybrid scheme exploits the high information content of the power spectrum, compressing both the power spectrum and neural-based summaries that are designed to extract further information. Our simulation-based approach enables principled forward modelling of all major sources of systematic uncertainty and survey properties into realistic mock observations, including the survey mask, photometric redshift uncertainties, intrinsic galaxy alignments, multiplicative shear calibration bias, source galaxy clustering, non-Gaussian shape noise, and non-linear structure formation. The summary statistics are then used in a Bayesian simulation-based inference pipeline. The inference is validated through coverage tests and checks for robustness against baryonic feedback. Assuming a $w$CDM cosmology, our analysis yields $S_8 = 0.808 \pm 0.017$, $\Omega_{\rm m} = 0.325 \pm 0.024$, and $w < -0.766$ (marginalized posterior 68 per cent credible intervals). This rigorous combination of information theory, physics- and neural network-based extreme data compression, and principled Bayesian analysis improves the figure of merit for $(\Omega_{\rm m}, S_8, w)$ by 60 per cent over the previous state-of-the-art, and by almost a factor of 3 over two-point analyses of the same data. They are the most precise joint constraints on $(\Omega_{\rm m}, S_8, w)$ from weak gravitational lensing data alone of any survey to date. We intend to apply this analysis to the more recent DES Y6 data.

item.title: Forward-modelling the Tolman and distance-duality tests with IllustrisTNG
item.description: arXiv:2606.27182v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Tolman surface-brightness test and the angular-size distance-duality test are two complementary probes of the same underlying relation between luminosity and angular-diameter distance, $D_L = (1+z)^2 D_A$, as holds in any metric theory of gravity where photon number is conserved. Both tests have recently delivered a priori surprising signals: JWST/ASTRODEEP measurements yield a surface brightness scaling with redshift much flatter than the expected value, and ultracompact radio sources also appear to follow a flatter $D_L/D_A$ scaling with redshift. These results have been suggested to support non-expanding cosmologies, however they are also sensitive to astrophysical and instrumental effects. We test whether these results indicate genuine departures from standard cosmology by forward-modelling observed surface-brightness evolution in the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation, with an empirical mock-spectroscopic selection trained on ASTRODEEP. We show that the astrophysical evolution relevant for both tests may be effectively parametrised as a single power-law exponent for the luminosity density as a function of redshift, for which the simulation gives $\gamma=2.23\pm0.20$ across realistic aperture conventions. This value is approximately sufficient to explain both the Tolman and distance-duality signals within standard cosmology and galaxy formation physics, with a small discrepancy for the latter suggesting that radio AGN evolve slightly more strongly than bright galaxies.
item.dc:creator: Harry Desmond, Tariq Yasin, Richard Stiskalek, Sebastian von Hausegger

item.title: Constraining dark energy with complementary probes of large-scale structure
item.description: arXiv:2606.31977v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To observationally pin down the nature of dark energy, it is essential to consistently model cosmological perturbations in the presence of dark energy alongside the background expansion and constrain this joint theory space with a large array of complementary probes. Here, we achieve this by constraining a model in the Effective Field Theory of Dark Energy (EFTofDE) framework by supplementing probes of the expansion history with several probes of large-scale structure: redshift space distortions (RSD) from DESI DR1, $3\times2$pt measurements from DES Y3, and the Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect from cross-correlating CMB temperature anisotropies with galaxy number counts or CMB lensing. We demonstrate the complementarity of different probes which leads to strong improvements on constraints on DE perturbations. For our most constraining dataset combination that supplements CMB+BAO+SNe probes with DESI DR1 RSD, DES Y3 $3\times2$pt and ISW cross-correlations between CMB temperature and galaxy counts, we find an improvement in the Figure of Merit (FoM) for the DE perturbation parameters $\{c_B, c_M\}$ by a factor of 2.69. We show the phenomenological implications of these constraints by mapping them to the present-day values of the phenomenological functions $\{\mu(z), \Sigma(z)\}$, where we see an FoM improvement by a factor of 3.37. We find a significant interdependence between the posteriors of $\{w_0, w_a\}$ and $\{c_B, c_M\}$, caused by the theoretical prior imposed by the gradient stability condition within the EFTofDE framework. Finally, we compute the significance of deviation from $\Lambda$CM for the EFTofDE model when constrained with CMB+BAO+SNe datasets, finding it to be at 2.9$\sigma$. This significance is nontrivially similar to the significance for the $w_0w_a$CDM model for the same dataset combination which we find to be 3.1$\sigma$.
item.dc:creator: Neel Shah, Kazuya Koyama, Johannes Noller, Lanyang Yi

item.title: The dark matter halo mass function in the $\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}$ cosmology at all times and over all scales -- from planetary to galaxy cluster masses
item.description: arXiv:2607.05505v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dark matter halo mass function is one of the most fundamental predictions of structure formation theory and cosmological simulations. We present the full halo mass function in the $\Lambda$ cold dark matter ($\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}$) model, ranging from a planetary mass ($10^{-6}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$; the thermal cutoff in the initial power spectrum for a fiducial CDM particle mass of $100\,\mathrm{GeV}$) to the mass of a rich galaxy cluster ($10^{15.5}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$), and from redshift, $z=30$ to the present. To span this very large dynamic range, we combine our earlier Voids-within-Voids-within-Voids (VVV) set of simulations (Wang et al) with large volume, lower resolution cosmological simulations. We develop a subsampling method to extract subvolumes from the original simulations, allowing us to reconstruct the global halo mass function from the biased underdense VVV regions. We show that the results agree reasonably well among the sets of simulations on different scales and environments. We provide a fitting formula for the dark matter halo mass function based on the work of Reed et al. calibrated with our simulations, such that it can be applied at all scales, all environments and all times, with deviations of $\sim2-3\%$ at $z < 2$ and $\sim 7\%$ at higher redshift $z \gtrsim 5$. This formula is also accurate at least for a restricted set of models we tested with modest deviations from $\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}$ in the values of some of the cosmological parameters. A python code is publicly available at https://github.com/haonan-zheng/hmfc.
item.dc:creator: Haonan Zheng, Sownak Bose, Carlos S. Frenk, Liang Gao, Adrian Jenkins, Shihong Liao, Yizhou Liu, Volker Springel, Jie Wang, Simon D. M. White

item.title: The One-Loop Power Spectrum of Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measures
item.description: arXiv:2608.03235v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fast radio burst (FRB) dispersion measures trace free electron column densities and will soon offer a unique probe of low-$z$ baryons. Such measurements can constrain cosmology directly, with the free electrons serving as a new tracer of large-scale structure, and probe the baryonic feedback of galaxies, a leading systematic for weak lensing surveys such as LSST and Euclid. We prepare for both science cases using effective field theory (EFT) and hydrodynamical simulations. We construct the one-loop EFT description of the free-electron auto-spectrum $P_{ee}$ and electron-galaxy cross-spectrum $P_{eg}$, placing FRB dispersion clustering on the same theoretical footing as spectroscopic galaxy analyses, and quantify the FRB densities at which this modeling is useful. We also investigate suitable galaxy samples for cross-correlations, finding that current spectroscopic catalogs provide appropriate redshift range and sufficient density. We validate the model against the FLAMINGO simulations, jointly fitting $P_{ee}$, $P_{eg}$, and $P_{gg}$ for DESI-like samples at $z=0.2$ and 0.5. The model describes all three spectra to $k\sim0.2\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, with an electron linear bias $b_{e,1}\simeq0.92$, higher-order biases consistent with zero, and all parameters stable across feedback variants. Together with the near-perfect electron-matter correlation $r_{em}\simeq1$, this establishes free electrons as nearly unbiased, feedback-robust tracers of matter, supporting a key assumption of FRB-based feedback constraints. These properties make electron clustering an ideal application for Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT), which would extend the modeling reach by a further factor of 2--3. The low-$z$ electron spectrum becomes signal-dominated beyond the linear regime within the first few years of next-generation surveys; the models developed here will be necessary on these timescales.
item.dc:creator: Haruki Ebina, Martin White

item.title: Modified Expansion and the JWST CMB Optical Depth Tension in Cosmology inspired by Self-Interaction Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2608.03470v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent JWST observations suggests an earlier and more efficient reionization history, and thus larger Thomson optical depths than inferred from the from the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We test whether a modified expansion history motivated by self-interaction (SI) gravity can reduce this tension while retaining the standard astrophysical description of reionization. The parameters of an SI-motivated depletion function are constrained with a Bayesian MCMC using Union3 Type Ia supernovae, DESI DR2 BAO, and the CMB acoustic scale $(\theta_*)$. We then compute the ionization history and optical depth, including cosmology-dependent remapping of UV luminosity functions. The predicted optical depth drops from $\tau_{\rm CMB}=0.0745\pm0.0001$ in $\Lambda$CDM to $\tau_{\rm CMB} = 0.0643 \pm 0.001$ in the SI-motivated background. This shifts agreement with Planck PR3 to $\sim1.4\sigma$, versus $\sim3\sigma$ in $\Lambda$CDM, easing the tension. While the SI-motivated model slightly improves the best fit to the combined data, information criteria show no significant preference over $\Lambda$CDM.
item.dc:creator: Subhadeep Mukherjee, Shashank Shekhar Pandey, A. S. Majumdar

item.title: Mean-Field Backreaction in Single-Field Inflation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26669v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The validity of linear perturbation theory and the role of backreaction in single-field inflationary models that enhance power at small scales have recently been under debate. We investigate scalar backreaction semi-analytically in a mean-field approach within the decoupling limit, considering popular models with a transient ultra-slow-roll (USR) stage or an oscillatory feature (OF) in the potential. We find that ultraviolet (UV) modes in the Bunch--Davies vacuum can substantially affect backreaction estimates unless removed by adiabatic subtraction. Our mean-field treatment can reproduce recent lattice results, but reveals a spurious sensitivity to UV contributions in some cases. This sensitivity is reduced in the OF model when copious particle production separates the amplified physical modes from the UV vacuum tail, making lattice results more reliable in this regime. In USR, instead, adiabatically subtracted spectra yield milder backreaction on the background evolution than previously inferred.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Braglia, Gabriele Franciolini, Nadir Ijaz, Marco Peloso

item.title: Breaking the background and linear degeneracies: Using nonlinear clustering to discriminate between dark energy models
item.description: arXiv:2611.26460v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the traditional approach of parameterizing the background and linear-perturbation evolutions, through the equation-of-state parameter $w(a)$ and a time-dependent sound speed squared $\bar{c}^2_s(a)$, does not fully specify the cosmological behavior of dark energy theories. Using a new, fully nonlinear fluid framework, we perform spherical-collapse simulations of two clustering dark energy models with identical $w(a)$ and $\bar{c}^2_s(a)$, finding that their central dark-energy densities differ by up to 50\% for cluster-sized dark matter halos. We identify the departure of the local sound speed from $\bar{c}_s$ as the main driver of these differences. In contrast, all other theory-specific quantities in the fluid equations can be described by their background values to a very good approximation. The results demonstrate that nonlinear structure formation encodes critical additional information about the underlying dark energy theory, opening an avenue for discriminating between models using observables on small scales.
item.dc:creator: Yunhao Gao, Baojiu Li, Jie Wang, Carlton M. Baugh

item.title: Splitting the action: A fully nonlinear fluid method for clustering dark energy
item.description: arXiv:2611.26461v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While the background evolution of dark energy is relatively straightforward to model, its perturbations, especially on nonlinear scales, generally require significantly more sophisticated treatment. Existing simulation methods for clustering dark energy --- a large class of interesting theories which are until now not well studied --- usually rely on grid-based solvers and perturbatively derived equations, whose validity in the nonlinear regime remains unknown. In this paper, we introduce a novel fluid method based on splitting the dark energy action into two parts: a kinetic part and a potential part. The resulting fluid equations are fully nonlinear and not reliant on simplifying approximations, making them suitable to describe the small-scale evolution of clustering dark energy theories, such as $k$-essence models with small sound speeds. We demonstrate the numerical implementation of this framework through spherical-collapse simulations of two representative $k$-essence models, evolving dark matter and dark energy simultaneously. The simulations are able to follow the development of dark-energy density perturbations throughout halo collapse, to $\mathcal{O}(\textrm{1}-10)$. By investigating their dependence on the dark-energy sound speed and dark-matter halo mass, we illustrate how dark-energy clustering responds to variations in the competing effects of pressure support and gravitational pull. These results demonstrate the applicability of this new framework to study nonlinear dark-energy clustering across a range of physical conditions, providing the foundation for its future extension to fully three-dimensional cosmological simulations through particle-based algorithms such as smooth particle hydrodynamics (SPH).
item.dc:creator: Yunhao Gao, Baojiu Li, Jie Wang, Carlton M. Baugh

item.title: Star-forming disc galaxies align tangentially with the cosmic tidal field
item.description: arXiv:2611.26593v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The alignments of galaxy shapes, with one another and with the large-scale structure of the Universe, have been a topic of considerable investigation within cosmology and extragalactic astrophysics for the last 60 years. Galaxy alignments are a major systematic for weak gravitational lensing and help us learn about the processes of galaxy formation. Red early-type galaxies are known to show strong radial alignments around other galaxies; however, blue star-forming galaxies have shown little evidence of alignment. We combine SPHEREx spectrophotometry with DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys to build a full-sky catalogue of 71 million galaxies with precise redshifts. With this catalogue we are able to measure alignment signals by splitting galaxies into colour and morphological samples. We detect tangential alignment of blue disc galaxies at $22.5\sigma$ and radial alignment of red spheroidal galaxies at $65\sigma$. By measuring the alignment signal separately around overdensities and underdensities, we show that each of these alignments has the scale and environmental dependence of a linear response to the cosmic tidal field; a response purely quadratic in the Gaussian tidal field, as in classic tidal torque theory is ruled out.
item.dc:creator: Calum Murray, Roman Paviot, Martin Kilbinger, Cail Daley, Ken Ganga, Michael J. Hudson

item.title: Effects of dark dipole radiation on eccentric supermassive black hole binary inspirals
item.description: arXiv:2510.08514v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The final-parsec problem has long posed a central challenge in understanding the merger of supermassive black hole binaries. In this paper, we investigate a scenario in which a dark scalar or vector field is sourced by eccentric binaries, leading to accelerated mergers through additional dipole radiation, and thereby extending the range of masses for which the binary can merge within a Hubble time. The Newtonian-order radiation fluxes from an eccentric charged Keplerian binary are derived using general results for localized periodic sources in flat spacetime. We find that dipole radiation, although insufficient to fully resolve the final-parsec problem, can alter the low-frequency spectrum of the stochastic gravitational wave background from supermassive black hole binary inspirals. We construct a simplified model for the spectrum and perform a Bayesian analysis using the current pulsar timing array data.
item.dc:creator: Mu-Chun Chen, Yan Cao

item.title: Correlation Calibration: A Hybrid Calibration Technique for Radio Interferometric Arrays
item.description: arXiv:2602.06109v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Calibrating out per-antenna signal chain effects is an essential step in analyzing radio interferometric data. For drift-scanning arrays, robustly calibrating the data is especially challenging due to the lack of the ability to track a calibration source. Consequently, calibration strategies for drift-scanning arrays are limited by our knowledge of the radio sky at large, as well as the direction-dependent instrument response. In the context of 21 cm cosmology, where small calibration errors can conspire to overwhelm the cosmological signal, it is therefore crucially important to develop calibration strategies that are capable of accurately calibrating the data in the presence of sky or instrument modeling errors. In this paper we present CorrCal, a covariance-based calibration strategy for radio interferometric arrays. CorrCal is a hybrid calibration strategy that leverages the strengths of traditional sky-based calibration and redundant calibration in a computationally efficient framework that is fairly insensitive to modeling errors. We find that calibration errors from CorrCal are unbiased and far below typical thermal noise thresholds across a wide range of modeling error scenarios. We show that CorrCal is computationally efficient: our implementation is capable of evaluating the likelihood and its gradient in less than a second for 1,000-element class arrays using just a single laptop core. Given CorrCal's computational efficiency and robustness to modeling errors, we anticipate that it will serve as a useful tool in the analysis of radio interferometric data from current and next-generation experiments targeting the cosmological 21 cm signal.
item.dc:creator: Robert Pascua, Jonathan Sievers, Adrian Liu

item.title: Measuring the Angular Auto-power Spectrum of Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measures as a Cosmological Probe and Baryon Tracer
item.description: arXiv:2607.04106v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fluctuations in the cosmic electron density are imprinted on the dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs), making DMs a promising probe of cosmology and the spatial distribution of ionized baryons. In this work, we present the first measurement of the angular auto-power spectrum of FRB DMs, using 3455 apparently non-repeating bursts from the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2. We detect an angular correlation signal at $\sim 2.8 \sigma$ significance, associated with large-scale electron-density fluctuations. By fitting the measured spectrum to theoretical models, we constrain two key parameter combinations: $\Omega_{\rm b}h^2$-$H_0$, which probes the cosmic baryon density and expansion rate, and $\Omega_{\rm b}h^2$-$f_{\rm d}$, which traces the baryon fraction in cosmic large-scale structure (LSS). We further assess the sensitivity of the power-spectrum method to systematic uncertainties arising from the assumed FRB redshift distribution and from the DM contributions of host galaxies (${\rm DM}_{\rm host}$), the Galactic halo (${\rm DM}^{\rm MW}_{\rm halo}$), and the Milky Way interstellar medium (${\rm DM}^{\rm MW}_{\rm ISM}$), using mock samples. Our results demonstrate that the angular power spectrum is largely insensitive to uncorrelated DM components such as ${\rm DM}_{\rm host}$, thereby effectively mitigating the impact of poorly constrained host-galaxy systematics. In contrast to the mean ${\rm DM}_{\rm LSS}$-$z$ relation, this method does not require individual redshift measurements but relies only on the overall redshift distribution, and partially breaks the parameter degeneracies in the $\Omega_{\rm b}h^2$-$H_0$ and $\Omega_{\rm b}h^2$-$f_{\rm d}$ planes. These findings establish the DM angular power spectrum as a reliable cosmological probe and a powerful baryon tracer.
item.dc:creator: Bao Wang, Zhiyu Lu, Yang Liu, Jun-Jie Wei, Xue-Feng Wu

item.title: XRISM Reveals a Kinematically Coherent Core System of the Nearby Cool-Core Cluster Abell 2199
item.description: arXiv:2607.06977v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present the results of a deep 251 ks XRISM/Resolve observation of the cool core of the galaxy cluster Abell 2199. From the integrated spectrum of the central $3' \times 3'$ Resolve field of view ($104 \times 104 \mathrm{~kpc}^2$), we find that the intracluster medium (ICM) redshift is consistent with that of the brightest cluster galaxy, within the optical-redshift uncertainty. This indicates that they form a kinematically coherent core system, which is offset from the mean cluster redshift by $\sim200~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$. The observed velocity dispersion of $\sim100~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$ corresponds to a three-dimensional Mach number of $M_{\mathrm{3D}}=0.16$ and a non-thermal pressure fraction of $P_{\mathrm{NT}}/P_{\mathrm{tot}}=1.4\pm0.2$%. Abell 2199 is one of the most dynamically quiescent relaxed clusters observed with XRISM, despite the presence of radio jets and a plume-like structure possibly associated with sloshing motions. Order-of-magnitude estimates suggest that turbulent dissipation could offset a non-negligible fraction of the radiative cooling losses, with $Q_{\mathrm{turb}}/Q_{\mathrm{cool}}\approx0.1$ for a large-scale driver such as sloshing and larger values for smaller AGN-feedback scales. Finally, we detect a localized enhancement of the Fe XXV He$\alpha$ $y$ line in the southeast region, which spatially coincides with a Chandra surface brightness discontinuity.
item.dc:creator: Kazunori Suda, Kyoko Matsushita, Kosuke Sato, Kotaro Fukushima, Ming Sun, Caroline Kilbourne, John A. ZuHone, Edmund Hodges-Kluck, Shogo B. Kobayashi, Simon Dupourque, Daniel R. Wik, Priyanka Chakraborty, Arnab Sarkar, Marie Kondo, Itsuki Aihara, Eric D. Miller, Francois Mernier

item.title: Formation and scaling of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ strings for global $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2607.21701v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We numerically investigate networks of global $\mathbb{Z}_N$ strings with multi-string junctions in a scalar field model whose vacuum manifold is $\mathrm{PSU}(N)=\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathbb{Z}_N$. The construction of the model is motivated by the Higgs vacua of mass-deformed $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory, commonly known as $\mathcal{N}=1^*$ theory, and provides a tractable effective description of string networks with baryon-vertex-like junctions. We perform classical lattice simulations of the formation and evolution of these networks in a radiation-dominated universe. For $N=2,3,$ and $4$, the time histories suggest that the total winding-length density approaches approximate scaling over the simulated interval, with no evidence for frustration. For $N=5$ and $8$, we report densities at selected times. For the parameters studied, the density normalization grows approximately in proportion to $N^2-1$, while non-minimal-charge components remain subdominant.
item.dc:creator: Masaki Yamada

item.title: Equivalence of mapping gravitational wave background anisotropy across bases at equal information content
item.description: arXiv:2608.05200v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mapping anisotropies in the gravitational-wave background (GWB) requires choosing a basis to represent the sky intensity, such as pixel and spherical harmonic bases. Each introduces a truncation---e.g., a number of pixels or a maximum multipole l_max---often set by a naive counting argument that relate the number of measurable modes to the number of independent cross-correlations, N_pair, in a pulsar timing array (PTA). However, such truncations can lead to reconstruction artifacts, as they do not reflect the true information content of the PTA response. Increasing the value of truncation parameters spans the observable space better but reveals poorly constrained modes, making the inverse problem ill conditioned and requiring regularization. A natural approach is to restrict the reconstruction to a well-measured subspace via principal maps, defined by the dominant eigenmodes of the detector response (or Fisher) matrix. However, these maps are not a fundamental parametrization of the sky but, rather, are derived from an underlying representation---such as a pixelization or a spherical harmonic expansion. While their explicit form depends on basis choice, they can span the \textit{same subspace} when the underlying representation is sufficiently complete. Here, we show that reconstructed anisotropy maps via different bases are equivalent, provided they retain the same information content, i.e., span the same principal subspace. As illustrative cases, we consider a toy model for PTA configuration and several GWB anisotropy shapes: point source, an extended source with deterministic anisotropy, and a statistical isotropic background, along with its summary statistic---the angular power spectrum. Although the reconstructions are equivalent, their computational costs can differ. We conclude with brief comments on the construction of principal maps for ground-based interferometers.
item.dc:creator: Deepali Agarwal

item.title: Massive de Sitter Correlators as Finite Mellin-Barnes Integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.10921v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using the Mellin-Barnes representation of de Sitter propagators, we reduce tree-level heavy-particle exchange to finite integrals that converge at physical kinematics on mass-independent contours, and one-loop diagrams to the same integrand times a flat-space momentum factor. We compute the complete one-loop triangle at general masses, with its collider signal in closed form to all orders in the squeezed-limit expansion, and give the triple-exchange bispectrum at arbitrary heavy masses as a double series that converges at every physical shape. The loop reduction also applies at strong mixing.
item.dc:creator: Amara McCune

item.title: Inelastic Kinetic Decoupling in WIMP Leptogenesis: A Minimal $Z_4$ Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.38531v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a minimal $Z_4$-symmetric extension of the Standard Model in which a singlet Dirac fermion $\chi$ constitutes dark matter, whose annihilations generate a lepton asymmetry through WIMP leptogenesis. Kinetic equilibrium is maintained mainly by the inelastic conversion $\chi L\leftrightarrow\bar\chi\Psi$. Compared with the near elastic regime, a sizable mass gap suppresses the conversion rate more rapidly as the Universe cools. This naturally drives kinetic decoupling to earlier times, even away from resonance. Starting from the full inelastic collision operator, we derive an effective momentum transfer rate for kinetic decoupling. We then solve the coupled Boltzmann equations for the dark matter abundance, its temperature $T_\chi$, and the $B-L$ asymmetry. Early kinetic decoupling can significantly modify the relic abundance, although near resonance this modification can be reduced by annihilation-induced heating. The $B-L$ asymmetry can be affected when asymmetry production overlaps with a substantial departure from kinetic equilibrium. In our scan, the largest deviations occur mainly for $x_{\rm lep}\gtrsim x_{\rm cd}$. After imposing our constraints, asymmetry production typically ends before chemical decoupling, leaving the final asymmetry essentially unchanged. For indirect detection, we generate the photon spectrum with Pythia and evaluate the Fermi-LAT dwarf spheroidal likelihood.
item.dc:creator: An Liu, Hong-Hao Zhang

item.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) A: Strong lens catalogue overview
item.description: arXiv:2611.15883v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present 15 072 high-confidence strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), spanning 2000 deg$^2$. These comprise 6073 grade A ('sure lens') and 8999 grade B ('probable lens') systems, which we publish alongside a further 9010 grade C ('possible lens') candidates. With more high-confidence candidates than all previous catalogues combined, this sample establishes a large, homogeneous data set of galaxy-scale strong lenses with high-resolution imaging, transforming strong lensing from a field of rare discoveries to a robust statistical tool for astrophysics and cosmology. Of the roughly 900 million sources in DR1, we searched the 68 million passing our catalogue selection using a bespoke discovery pipeline that synthesises scores from five machine-learning models with visual classifications from around 7000 citizen scientists and 67 strong lensing experts. Beyond classical Einstein rings, our catalogue includes 84 candidate double-source-plane lenses and over 1000 candidate disc lenses, two exotic classes with few previously known examples, as well as several hundred candidate lensed AGN and quasars. We deliver automated lens models for the combined grade A+B systems, and photometric redshifts and stellar population properties for the deflector galaxies, providing immediate science-ready data products. We find that the majority of the deflector galaxies are massive and quiescent, with stellar masses of $\log_{10}(M_\ast /M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$ (Salpeter initial mass function; 16th-84th percentile range). The deflector galaxies span a range of photometric redshifts ($z=0.68 ^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$), extending to higher redshifts than previous ground-based lens samples, and the lenses have a typical Einstein radius of $0.85 ^{+0.44}_{-0.24}$ arcsec. Extrapolating by area, we expect over 100 000 high-confidence strong lens candidates in the Euclid Wide Survey.

item.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) B: Discovery pipeline overview
item.description: arXiv:2611.15886v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present the method used to identify the $15\,000$ high-grade galaxy-galaxy strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Given that lenses are intrinsically rare systems and the DR1 data set is vast, this lens search was conducted in a number of stages: a catalogue-level cut; a machine-learning and ensemble search; a two-stage citizen-science search, and finally grading of lens candidates by strong lens researchers. In this paper, we describe each search stage and their respective results. This search was enabled by the automated classification of over 68 million objects by neural networks, more than 4.5 million classifications of $300\,000$ objects by citizen-scientist volunteers, and the inspection of over $30\,000$ objects by strong lens researchers. We find this multi-stage approach helps maximise the number of lenses identified, while minimising inspection requirements of both citizen scientists and strong lens researchers. We measure a completeness in our comprehensive search of $0.73_{-0.15}^{+0.08}$ to grade A ('definite') systems and $0.34_{-0.06}^{+0.05}$ to grade A+B ('definite' + 'probable') systems. Our search therefore identifies the majority of the definitive strong lens systems in the DR1 area with the remainder likely to be fainter or more ambiguous cases. We find that researcher grading remains subjective; in this work we implement calibration to account for biases of individual inspectors and highlight the benefit of lens modelling (ECLIPSE-C) in determining the nature of a lens candidate. This paper forms part of the ECLIPSE series, here focussing on the discovery pipeline used to identify lens candidates in Euclid DR1; an overview of the lenses discovered is presented in ECLIPSE-A.

item.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Calibration strategy and observations
item.description: arXiv:2611.16546v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper reviews how Euclid's top-level calibration requirements were translated into a calibration plan, how this plan is implemented and maintained during the survey, and how it performs in the current DR1 release. We show that DR1 already meets or exceeds most end-of-mission spectrophotometric calibration requirements. The construction of spectroscopically complete and pure samples relies on ongoing data acquisition for the Euclid Deep Survey, while point-spread-function modelling and shear calibration are still converging to their stringent accuracy requirements. With all DR1 data reprocessed with the DR1 pipeline configuration, more subtle effects have been detected and characterised, and correction strategies have been developed for DR2. These include improved absolute flux calibration, astrometry, charge-persistence correction, shutter effects, wavelength calibration, and spectrophotometric corrections for water-ice contamination. Finally, synthetic photometric transformations between Euclid and each of Roman, the James Webb Space Telescope, and the Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope, are presented.

item.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Spacecraft performance in the L2 environment
item.description: arXiv:2611.16548v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Euclid mission was designed around the need for thermo-optical and mechanical stability, stray-light suppression, low outgassing, and precise guiding. After three years in space, a wealth of data is available to assess the performance in these areas. We review the L2 halo-orbit design and consumables budget. Solar stray-light gradually increases by 14% per year and is consistent with meteoroid puncturing, but remains low overall. Data loss from high solar activity has declined notably since the maximum of the 25th Solar cycle passed. The thermodynamical response of the optical elements to a thermal step impulse follows sigmoidal growth curves, entering the asymptotic equilibration regime after 21--46 hours. Water-ice contamination has affected data from both instruments and requires continued monitoring; we review detection and decontamination methods, and Euclid's contamination history. High-precision measurements of the zodiacal background reveal, at eight sigma significance, the subtle modulation caused by the changing perspective on the dust distribution due to the L2 halo-orbit libration. These data also show that conservative pre-launch estimates overestimated the out-of-field stray-light by factors of 4 (H band) to 27 (I band). Telemetry data demonstrate excellent guiding, and enable highly significant detections of solar radiation pressure and of thermal-emission recoil from Euclid's unilluminated dark sides. Lastly, we present a list of 34 meteoroid impacts, discuss their mechanical and optical signatures, and derive a minimum detectable impactor mass of 5e-7 g.

item.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.18794v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about 6.6%.
item.dc:creator: Jing Zhou, Ligong Bian
